fields.h1: Build a Coaching Application Form That Screens Before the Call
fields.hero_description: Build a coaching application form that screens applicants before a discovery call and keeps every answer in your own database.
fields.features_heading: What a Coach Learns Before the First Call
fields.features_subheading: A coaching application form gives you the facts to decide who gets a discovery call. Each piece below handles one part of it.
fields.feature_1:
Questions that sort applicants by fit

Ask for the role, the goal, and how soon someone can start. Put a rule on any answer, such as team size, and the app tags each application as a fit or a maybe before you open it.
fields.feature_2:
A call link only for the right applicants

Applicants who meet your rule get a confirmation email with your scheduling link. Everyone else gets a reply that says when you will be in touch, and nobody waits without an answer.
fields.feature_3:
Seat limits with a waitlist behind them

Give a cohort or a client roster a fixed number of spots. Once the last one is taken, the form keeps accepting applications and places each new person on the waitlist in order.
fields.feature_4:
Alerts in Slack or your inbox

Send each new application to your inbox, or post it to a coaching channel in Slack. When an application sits unanswered for 2 days, the app sends you a reminder about it.
fields.feature_5:
Every applicant in a database you own

Each application is saved as a row in a database you own, with no response caps. Filter by goal or start date, and mark each person booked, waitlisted, or declined as you go.
fields.feature_6:
Code you can take with you

On paid plans, export the full codebase of the form and its database to your GitHub repository. Move it to your own hosting, or keep building on it as your practice grows.

fields.usecase_heading: Who Applies, and Who Gets the Call
fields.tab_content_1:
Philomena leads a team of 14 and gets the call link

Saffron Vale Leadership Coaching takes only clients who manage a team. Its form asks for name, role, team size, and a goal for the next 6 months. Philomena Corwen, a VP of operations, leads 14 people. Anyone leading 5 or more gets the discovery call link in the confirmation email, and hers arrives at once.
fields.tab_content_2:
When seat 12 fills, Marguerite tops a waitlist

Juniper Gate Career Coaching runs a 10-week career-change cohort with 12 seats. Its form asks for name, current field, target field, and a weekday evening. Marguerite Elsby, a pharmacist moving into UX research, applies after seat 12 is taken. She is first on the waitlist, and her answers are saved for the next cohort.
fields.tab_content_3:
With a race in 9 weeks, Linnea gets a flag

Isidore Lattimer coaches distance runners at Redfern Hill Running. His form asks for name, goal race, weeks to race day, weekly miles, and running days. Linnea Sato is 9 weeks from a marathon at 22 miles a week, running 4 days. Any race under 12 weeks away is flagged, which puts her at the top of his call list.
fields.tab_content_4:
Nine owners apply, and by Monday Augusta has the count

Every Monday, Augusta Rook opens one email counting the week's applications to Maplecrest Growth Coaching. Her form asks owners for name, business type, years in business, and the biggest bottleneck. This week, 9 owners applied. Four named hiring, 3 named sales, and 2 named pricing.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Coaching Application Form
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to build a coaching application form that asks what decides fit and sends each applicant to the right next step.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Write down who you coach best
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Ask only what decides the call
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Set the rule for each next step
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Count the clients you can take
fields.howto_step_1_des: List the clients you helped most in the last year, such as managers with a team or runners chasing a first marathon. What they have in common becomes your fit rules, and each question on the form exists to test one of them.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Tie every question to a decision. Team size decides who gets the call link, and weeks to race day decides who you phone first. Cut anything you would not act on, and leave payment details until after the call.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Write the rule in plain words, such as 5 or more direct reports gets the scheduling link. Then decide what everyone else receives: a reply within 3 business days, a referral to another coach, or a place on the waitlist.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Pick the number of clients or cohort seats you can coach well at one time, and put it in the prompt. Decide whether people who apply after that number is reached join a waitlist or see a closed message.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Describe it all in one prompt
fields.howto_step_5_des: Put the questions, the rules, and the spot limit into a single prompt. Emergent builds the coaching application form, the database behind it, and a screen for reviewing each applicant. Ask in plain English when a question needs changing later.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Send them to your inbox, or post them to a Slack channel if a partner screens with you. Add a weekly count too, like a Monday email that sorts the week's applicants by the bottleneck each one named.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Submit one application that meets your rule and one that does not, using a spare email address. Check that the first gets the call link, the second gets the right reply, and both land in the table with the correct status.

faq_plan.q: What is a coaching application form?
faq_plan.a: A coaching application form is the set of questions a prospective client answers before a coach agrees to work with them. The International Coaching Federation (ICF) defines coaching as partnering with clients in a thought-provoking and creative process. The form checks whether that partnership fits: the goal, the timing, and the answer that decides a discovery call.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a coaching application form?
faq_plan.a: Decide who you coach best, which answers show it, and what each applicant receives next. Describe that in one prompt to Emergent's AI form builder. It builds the form, the rules that sort applicants, and the database every application saves to. Submit two test applications before you share the link.

faq_plan.q: What questions belong on a coaching application form template?
faq_plan.a: Start with name and email, then the goal the person wants to reach and by when. Add their current situation, the hours they can give each week, and how they heard about you. Treat a coaching application form template as a draft: drop any question whose answer would not change your decision, and add the one that decides fit, such as team size.

faq_plan.q: How long should a coaching application form be?
faq_plan.a: Aim for 8 to 12 questions that someone can finish in about 5 minutes, with the goal question near the top. Save deeper questions for the discovery call itself. A vendor application can run longer, because it collects product and booth details that a coaching applicant never needs.

faq_plan.q: Should a coaching application form ask about budget?
faq_plan.a: Yes, if price decides who you take on. Offer ranges instead of an open box, and list your package prices on the page above the form. The question then reads as fair rather than as a test. If your prices are fixed and public, skip it and ask about weekly time instead.

faq_plan.q: How do I use a coaching application form to screen clients before a discovery call?
faq_plan.a: Write one rule for each thing that decides fit, then let the form apply it. Team size, a start date, or weeks to an event can each be tested from a single answer. Applicants who pass get your call link, and the rest get a reply or a waitlist place. Emergent builds those rules into the form from a plain-English prompt.

faq_plan.q: Can I use a coaching application form to recruit coaches?
faq_plan.a: Yes, for volunteer roles. A youth league's form for volunteer coaches can ask which age group they want, their years of experience, and two references. For a paid coaching position, use a job application form instead, with work history and the role applied for.

faq_plan.q: What should happen after someone submits a coaching application form?
faq_plan.a: Send a confirmation email at once that says what happens next and when. Anyone who passes your fit rule finds the call link in that email. Everyone else hears when you will reply, or where they stand on the waitlist. Then answer the rest within the time you promised.

faq_plan.q: Can a coaching application form limit how many clients I take?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Set a number of spots, and when the last one is taken, new applicants join a waitlist in the order they applied. Emergent puts no response caps on the form, and a busy month never closes it before you choose to.

faq_plan.q: Can a coaching application form capture a signature?
faq_plan.a: Yes, as a step at the end of the form. An app built with Emergent can capture an e-signature, such as agreement to your cancellation policy. Keep the full coaching agreement as its own document if it runs long. The same signature step works on a rental application form, where an applicant confirms their answers are true.
